Buddy uses Android\'s accessibility service to do what you ask in other apps: it reads what\'s on the screen and taps, types and scrolls for you. It also shows the floating bubble.

While a task runs, the screen content, which can include personal information such as messages, names or addresses, is sent to the AI service of the agent you choose (Anthropic for Claude Code, OpenAI for Codex, or your OpenCode model\'s provider), only to carry out your request.
Buddy has no servers of its own. It doesn\'t collect, sell or share this data, and doesn\'t use it for ads.
Before anything that sends, posts, buys or deletes, Buddy asks for your OK. You can turn the service off anytime in Android\'s accessibility settings.
Paused for 5 minutes, so Buddy stopped the task.
Stopped. Your phone is yours again.

Paused because you touched the screen. Tap Paused next to the bubble to resume.

Buddy\'s phone tools are a regular MCP server on this phone. Run this once in a terminal on the phone (Termux, for example) and that agent gets the phone tools in every session, even without the bubble.
Copied. Paste it in your terminal.
Your phone\'s speech recognition (Google on most phones). Live text while you speak; detects which of your languages you\'re speaking.
Your phone\'s text-to-speech voices, in the reply\'s language.
Tap to choose the languages you speak. Long-press one to make it the default. In a chat, long-press the mic to switch language.

Opens the chat full screen in Buddy. Hold the bubble for more.
Full goes edge to edge. Compact is smaller and keeps clear of the screen edges, so side gestures keep working.
One tap opens the mic: say what you want and it sends when you pause. Hold the bubble for the chat and more.

The bubble\'s agent may run commands and edit files in Termux with Claude Code\'s full tools, so it can build and install apps.
For testing Buddy with an agent (for example Claude Code in Termux with the phone tools). The bubble, approval cards, App permissions and these switches stay off-limits.

Leave it off for everyday use: with it on, a malicious message or web page on screen could try to trick the agent into running commands. Approval cards still guard sending, posting, buying and deleting.
Every Claude Code and Codex session on this phone.
Buddy\'s accessibility service is off, so sessions can\'t be checked. Turn it on in Settings.
Runs in Claude Code\'s background service, e.g. a chat you continue from the Claude app.
It runs in the background, for example a chat you\'re continuing from the Claude app. It could even be the one controlling Buddy. Stopping it ends that conversation\'s current work.
It may be a session you\'re using in a terminal right now. It could even be the one controlling Buddy. Stopping it ends that conversation\'s current work.

Trust: the agent works on its own here, with no approval popups.
Hard: your button rules decide. Send, Pay, Delete… need your OK on a card.
Smart: the rules, then a separate reviewer AI checks every other tap against your request.
The agent can never tap Buddy's own bubble, cards or settings.

A temporary session per tap, without tools: it sees your request, the agent\'s note and the screen, and says allow, ask you, or advise against. About 3 seconds a tap. OpenCode chats are reviewed by Claude Code (or Codex).
It also checks replies before a notification rule\'s countdown sends them.
For apps on Hard or Smart. A rule picked from the suggestions applies to that app; typed text applies to all apps. Tap a rule to remove it.
Send, Post, Pay, Buy, Order, Delete, Call, Log out… always ask, in every language Buddy is translated into.
Buttons the agent taps in Hard and Smart apps show up here.

When a notification you pick arrives, Buddy gives your instruction to an agent, like a message you\'d type. Notifications that no rule matches are ignored.
Buddy needs it to see the notifications your rules watch.
Turn off to pause every rule.
No rules yet. For example: when a customer writes to you on WhatsApp, reply with your opening hours.
Skipped: too many in the last hour.
Waiting: too many in the last hour. The new messages get one run together at %1$s.
Most runs an hour for one conversation, and three times as many for the whole rule. Past it, new messages wait and then get one run together. Off: no limit.
Skipped: the phone was busy for too long.

Approval cards wait for you, as in any chat.

When the countdown ends, the card approves itself unless you tap to stop it. That only works for sending a message, after a second AI checks it against your rule. Paying, buying, deleting and opening links always wait for you.
Second AI: %1$s. Tap to change it in App permissions.
Buddy checks each notification against your rules. Notifications that no rule matches are ignored right away: not stored, not sent anywhere.
When one matches, its app, sender and text go to the rule\'s agent (Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode) together with your instruction.
Buddy can answer through a notification\'s Reply button. It asks you first, unless you give the rule a countdown.
